name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail in low-resolution frames without hallucinating artifacts, which directly boosts EXCAVA’s output sharpness—a 0.5%+ gain in perceived quality. The trade-off is compute overhead: depth-aware upscaling runs slower than standard methods, but the fidelity gain outweighs the speed drop for high-value outputs.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it targets resolution, not identity—faces still blur when the base model’s latent space collapses. Instead, test RealVisXL v1.1’s face model only on the final frame before export; if the face fidelity improves by 0.5%+ without overfitting artifacts, it’s the better lever. Settle it with a blind A/B test: run 100 frames through both pipelines and measure face sharpness vs. identity retention—no artifacts wins.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL v1.1’s face model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. Faces are EXCAVA’s weakest link—blur and identity drift kill perceived quality more than any other artifact. RealVisXL’s face model locks identity and sharpness where depth-aware upscaling can’t touch it, so the gain is real and immediate. The trade-off is speed: running a face model on every frame adds latency, but a 0.5%+ fidelity jump justifies it.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL v1.1’s face model risks overfitting to its synthetic training set—EXCAVA’s real-world faces will still drift because the model never saw them. Instead, test a hybrid: run RealVisXL’s face model *only* on the final frame, but pair it with a live identity-preserving upscaler (like GFPGAN 2.5) to lock the face before depth upscaling. If the face fidelity improves by 0.5%+ *without* overfitting artifacts, we’ll know it’s worth the compute cost.
